summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend federal offences for harming Australians overseas to conduct before 1 October 2002, allowing prosecutions concerning earlier incidents involving Australian citizens or residents.
It would remove the original commencement-date limit from the relevant offence provisions, covering murder, manslaughter and serious harm while retaining the division’s other criteria.
An application provision would expressly cover conduct before, on or after 1 October 2002, with the amendments starting the day after Royal Assent.
changes: The murder offence’s temporal coverage would extend to earlier overseas incidents.
The manslaughter offence’s temporal coverage would likewise extend to earlier incidents.
Serious harm offences would also become available for conduct predating the division.
summary.affected: Australian citizens and residents harmed overseas and people suspected of committing those offences are affected.

speeches.speaker: Nick Xenophon
speeches.brief: The speaker moved to introduce the Criminal Code Amendment (Harming Australians) Bill 2013, which amends the Criminal Code Act 1995, and the motion was agreed to.
